newsitem.title: JAPAN: Three Japan ministers have accounts with Nomura.
newsitem.headline: Three Japan ministers have accounts with Nomura.

text.p: Three ministers in Japan's cabinet currently have dealings with Nomura Securities Co Ltd but not in stocks and financial products in which the politicians could receive special treatment, the chief government spokesman said on Tuesday.
"The dealings were in government bonds and trust funds...none of which are instruments in which special favours could be granted," Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference.
"I will not make public the names, because they have nothing to do (with the Nomura payoff scandal)," Kajiyama said.
He said his check of the 20-member cabinet did not cover past transactions or accounts of the politicians' relatives.
"I have checked with the three ministers and there is no connection (to the Nomura payoff scandal)," Kajiyama said.
Asked if Nomura accounts in family members' names were included in the investigation, Kajiyama said: "I was not able to go as far as that."
He said his survey of the ministers "did not dig deeply into the past".
"The question is not whether in some form or another there were VIP accounts, but whether special favours were granted," Kajiyama said.
